title: Implement Dead-Letter Queue for Failed Records in Validation Service
description: The ChronoBoost Data Warehouse currently validates incoming data records in the `validation_service`. If a record fails validation against the schema, it is logged and discarded. This results in data loss and makes it difficult to debug ingestion problems. This task involves implementing a Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) pattern. Failed records, along with their validation error messages, should be persisted to a dedicated S3 bucket for later analysis and reprocessing.

project_spec.name: ChronoBoost Data Warehouse
project_spec.description:
ChronoBoost Data Warehouse is a high-throughput, serverless data-warehouse platform engineered to turbo-charge organisational productivity by turning raw operational exhaust into instantly actionable insights. Implemented in modern C and orchestrated entirely through serverless primitives, the solution ingests heterogeneous productivity data streams (calendar events, task changes, time-tracking logs, chat metrics, CI/CD telemetry) into an elastic Data Lake, continuously validates quality, and serves analytical aggregates and near-real-time dashboards without manual capacity planning.  

At its core, ChronoBoost couples a microservice mesh—compiled as lightweight, self-contained C binaries that boot inside custom AWS Lambda and Azure Functions runtimes—with an event-streaming backbone powered by managed Kafka and Kinesis. Each Lambda implements a single responsibility in the warehouse pipeline (ingestion, schema inference, batch compaction, quality scoring, strategy-pattern–based transformations, or Observer-pattern notifications). The end-to-end flow maximises knowledge-worker efficiency by providing zero-ops scalability, automatic error recovery, fine-grained monitoring, and proactive data-quality alerts delivered directly to productivity tools like Slack and Microsoft Teams.  

Advanced parallel processing and batch-window optimisation allow ChronoBoost to crunch millions of events in seconds while built-in data visualisation micro-frontends render key productivity KPIs—focus time, cycle time, meeting load, and delivery throughput—through interactive server-side–rendered SVG dashboards. All artefacts (66 source files, ~323k tokens) are organised under a clear pipeline pattern that developers can extend without downtime, ensuring the warehouse evolves alongside changing productivity goals.
dependencies: aws-sdk-cpp (AWS SDK for C++) — S3, Lambda, DynamoDB, Kinesis access
azure-core-c (Azure SDK for C) — optional multi-cloud function deployment
librdkafka (C client for Apache Kafka) — event streaming
Apache Arrow C library — columnar in-memory format for micro-batches
cJSON / RapidJSON — fast JSON parsing for productivity-tool payloads
libuv — cross-platform async I/O used in custom runtime
Prometheus C client — metrics exposition for monitoring
